To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

EBNA‐1 is required to maintain EBV as an extra‑chromosomal episome, that it is a key transcription factor in latent EBV infection, that it is the only viral protein that can link DNAs to each other and to metaphase chromosomes, that it binds cellular factors, and that it is the most immunogenic of the EBV nuclear proteins.

EBNA‐1 is a multifunctional protein that binds oriP, a 1.7 kb region within the EBV genome that is essential for viral replication, and that is required for the transcriptional activation of the latent genes in the viral genome.

the EBNA1 protein is a multifunctional protein that is required to replicate the Epstein Barr virus genome, to regulate the expression of viral latent genes and for viral transformation of human lymphocytes.
